description:
Two clauses that split on a guard over the head of a list nested inside two tuple levels fail on every path.

Program (scratchpad/ep5/probe/nested_list_head_guard.fz, stack base 62d660974):
  def deep({:a, {:b, [h | _]}}) when is_integer(h), do: 1
  def deep({:a, {:b, [h | _]}}) when is_atom(h), do: 2
  called as deep(pick_deep(n)), where pick_deep returns {:a, {:b, [n, n]}} or {:a, {:b, [:ok, :err]}}.

interp: 'backend executable ... function 77 clause 0 failed before entry 0: backend value was absent and cannot be materialized'.
run/build: 'error[artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan] ... native executable lowering failed', and the build path says 'native attempted to materialize absent value as runtime value with ty None'.

The same clauses one tuple level deep ({:a, [h | _]}) print 1 and 2 on interp and run. The guard can be is_atom(h) or h == :ok or h == :err; both fail.

Found by fz-ep5.2: fixture dispatch_nested_list_position_separates (functions deep and peed) passed while the head carried '::'. With the head moved to a guard it fails, so this blocks fz-ep5.2.

Not investigated: which job leaves the value absent, and whether a struct field or a list head under one tuple and one list behaves the same.

Fails before, passes after: the program above prints 1 then 2 on interp, run and build; dispatch_nested_list_position_separates passes with guards.
Acceptance: full gate green; no pin rises unexplained.
title: A guard on a list head two tuples deep compiles
